correctness.rationale: For extremal-width lattice segments A and B, mixed-area monotonicity implies v>=|det(A,B)|=d|b A_x-a B_x|. At 0<v<d the determinant vanishes. Primitive-direction lengths then equal at and bt, and v<b forces P to have zero integer transverse width, hence P is a segment. Its mixed area is a multiple of a; triangle constructions realize each permitted multiple. At ratio 3:5, the explicit semigroup, area-seven sheared pair, and small cases v=1,2,4 fill all attainable values; the low-area lemma forbids only the stated holes. The actual Python package produced 22200 exact integer-arithmetic checks. The proof, not the tests, establishes all infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Prescribed directional widths are central to the discrete Heine–Shephard problem, for which the motivating paper provides nonsharp gaps and an isolated special diagram. An exact forced-segment/divisibility law for every coprime reduced-width pair is a structural improvement, and the complete 3:5 section shows the sharp onset and permanence of the natural missing mixed area four. This is an exhaustive parameter classification, not a tiny numerical extension or recomputation of the prior single (30,50) table.
